hens_rule_text: Up to 20 head of poultry allowed on the first half acre of a lot (combined with rodents, no more than 25 total); the enclosure must be at least 80 ft from any residence unless the neighbor gives written permission for it to be closer, and never in the front yard.
permit_notes: No city permit for keeping hens. If the coop is closer than 80 ft to a neighbor's residence, written permission from that occupant and owner is required first.
setback_notes: 80 ft from any residence in the city, reducible with written neighbor consent. Arizona's 2024 state law (A.R.S. 9-462.12) separately guarantees up to six hens on lots of half an acre or less at single-family homes and caps any city setback at 20 ft with an 8 ft high, 200 sq ft enclosure limit for that guarantee, but Phoenix's own code already allows more (20 birds) than the state floor.
coop_rules: Enclosures must be built to keep poultry from wandering onto neighboring property and kept free of offensive smell or odor.
zoning_notes: Sec. 8-7 applies citywide, not by zone. No male poultry may be kept unless incapable of making vocal noise that disturbs the peace, which in practice rules out crowing roosters almost everywhere.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: Phoenix City Code Sec. 8-7, Poultry and rodents

Did not separately confirm whether any 2024-2026 amendment changed the 80 ft figure.
